text:
Looking at the diff: the `case 'second':` label (which grouped the singular "second" with `seconds`/`s` to return `n * s`) has been replaced with `case '':`.

Two things follow:

1. **`'second'` no longer matches.** The regex `(milliseconds?|msecs?|ms|seconds?|secs?|s|...)` happily matches the singular "second" (e.g. input `"1 second"` gives `match[2] === 'second'`). In the original code that hit `case 'second'` and returned `n * s`; in the patched code it falls through to `default:` and returns `undefined`. So `ms('1 second')` changed from `1000` to `undefined` — an observable change for any caller.

2. **`case '':` is dead code.** The unit group's alternatives all require at least one character, so `match[2]` is either `undefined` (no unit) or a non-empty string; `undefined` is converted to `'ms'` by `(match[2] || 'ms')`. An empty string can never reach the switch, so the replacement label never fires and doesn't compensate for anything.

The library's own tests evidently don't cover the singular "second", which is why the suite stays green.

```json
{"defect": true, "testFile": {"path": "proof-test.js", "content": "var assert = require('assert');\nvar ms = require('./');\n\ndescribe('proof', function () {\n  it('parses the singular unit \"second\"', function () {\n    assert.strictEqual(ms('1 second'), 1000);\n  });\n\n  it('parses singular \"second\" with a fractional value', function () {\n    assert.strictEqual(ms('1.5 second'), 1500);\n  });\n});\n"}, "note": "The diff removes the 'second' case label (replacing it with an unreachable empty-string case), so ms('1 second') now falls through to default and returns undefined instead of 1000. The regex still matches the singular 'second', so this is an observable regression."}
```
